Two direct attempts to measure gate 8 standalone under the Phase 1 harness (measure-gate-costs.sh --gate 8 --runs 2, and a raw run-all.sh --jobs 4 --timings run) were both contaminated mid-run by concurrent, unrelated sibling agent activity on the same host -- 1-minute load rose to 4.73-9.0 during the run, well above the harness's 2.0 threshold. Recovered by substituting a host-load-independent synthetic sleep-based concurrency probe (sleep is a kernel timer wait, immune to CPU contention) to answer the scheduler-concurrency question directly, and by relying on the already-idle-captured suite-cost-hints.txt for per-suite cost distribution instead of a fresh contaminated capture.

A synthetic sleep-based concurrency probe (N trivial sleep-6-and-exit suites run through the real, unmodified run-all.sh scheduler at --jobs 4/8/12/auto) conclusively discriminated the scheduler-concurrency and JOBS_CAP-binding candidates for gate 8's cost discrepancy without requiring an idle host at all, since sleep is immune to CPU contention. This is a reusable technique for any future scheduler-correctness question on a host that cannot be guaranteed idle.

git-commit-phase.sh's --objective flag intentionally narrows derivation to one objective's own files_touched array (its documented per-objective green-substep shape); the bare per-phase form unions every objective. This is working as designed, not a defect. The real gap: the completeness check (exit 6) validates only the DERIVED path set, so a per-objective call's narrowed derivation also narrows the completeness check, which therefore cannot warn about sibling-objective files the phase has already dirtied. This let 216 insertions across 3 files (gate_registry_exclude_ids, the full --skip-unchanged verify-deploy.sh wiring, and the .gitignore entry) sit committed-nowhere with no warning after a --objective-scoped commit, caught only by the orchestrator's own checkpoint audit rather than by the tool itself. Worth a future fix: have the completeness check additionally warn (non-blocking) when OTHER objectives in the same progress file carry files_touched entries that are still dirty against HEAD, even when derivation itself is correctly narrowed.

Used a made-up, never-registered objective id ('10b') in a git-commit-phase.sh --objective call. The wrapper correctly derived an empty files_touched set and printed a non-fatal 'nothing to derive' warning, which was misread as benign; the real source diff (gate-cache-lib.sh's scripts/lib/ implementation-digest memoization) was never staged, only the progress-file edit landed. Caught by a routine git diff recheck before closing the phase, not by the tool itself, and fixed via an explicit-pathspec git-commit-scoped.sh commit. Lesson: always pass a real, already-registered objective id, or omit --objective for a phase-closing union commit, and treat any 'nothing to derive' warning as a signal to verify git status immediately rather than routine noise.
